issues.body: `_live_issue_labels` validates that `labels` is a list but filters out any element that is not a dict with a string `name`. The result is then used as complete negative evidence by `_assert_status_landed`: a malformed entry is indistinguishable from proof that a dropped status label is gone. For example, a response such as `{"labels":[null,{"name":"role:impl"}]}` lets a removal-only transition pass even though the API response is not readable enough to establish the absence of every dropped label. This contradicts the helper's fail-closed confirmation purpose. The added unreadable-reread test only returns a malformed top-level string, so it remains green if nested entries continue to be discarded.
issues.fix_hint: Require every element of `item["labels"]` to be an object with a string `name`; raise `WorkerIssueError` on the first malformed element. Add a self-test that supplies a labels list containing a malformed element after a status write and asserts a diagnosable `cannot be confirmed` refusal.
issues.title: Malformed label entries are silently treated as absent

verdict.summary: The delete-before-add ordering and live postcondition are otherwise sound, but the new confirmation reader does not fail closed on malformed entries inside GitHub's labels array. Because it silently drops every non-object label and every object whose name is not a string, it can accept an incompletely readable response as proof that all removed labels are absent. The unreadable-response self-test exercises only a malformed top-level object and therefore does not catch this path. This is a new major finding relative to round 1's clean approval, so progress is regressing.
